topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the core learning objectives of the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: genetic mechanisms, environmental exposures, and chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of cancer development by exploring intrinsic mutations, microenvironmental requirements, inherited predisposition, and the epidemiological debate over environmental exposure versus random chance.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the oncogenic mechanisms of infectious agents, using the etiology and geographic distribution of Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens—including dietary toxins, combustion products, and xenobiotically metabolized compounds—cause direct and indirect DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, host susceptibility, and mechanisms of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how non-mutagenic tumor promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and host developmental timing collaborate with initiating mutations to facilitate malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and evaluating risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental strategies used to detect carcinogenic agents and assess their real-world risks.

topics.label: Conclusion and lecture summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic delivers the final summary and concluding thoughts on cancer causation and carcinogen risk evaluation.
